impact.cost_note: Most fixes use tools already in place. New monthly cost is limited to a missed-call text-back feature (price needs verification).

summary.pain: Missed calls at peak times, repeated "where's my technician" calls, and invoices typed twice are consuming office time and letting urgent callers slip away, in a business with a loyal maintenance-plan base and a scheduling system the team already knows.
summary.outcome: Turning on features of the existing stack and repairing one broken integration can return about 6 office hours per week and stop maintenance-plan renewals from lapsing, without a platform migration.

pain_points.title: Missed calls at peak times
pain_points.evidence: People calling about a no-heat don't leave voicemails, they call the next company.

pain_points.title: Technician status calls
pain_points.evidence: Ten, fifteen calls a day in the busy season... It's the same loop every time.

pain_points.title: Invoices typed twice
pain_points.evidence: The sync was set up years ago and it broke and nobody fixed it. So everything gets typed twice.

pain_points.title: Plan renewals lapsing
pain_points.evidence: We had a bunch of plans lapse last year because nobody reached out for the renewal.

pain_points.title: Slow quotes, no follow-up
pain_points.evidence: Some quotes take two or three days to go out. We don't really follow up on them.

pain_points.title: Manual Monday report
pain_points.evidence: Takes him most of the morning. I'd want it quicker, not fancier.

recommendations.title: Automatic "On My Way" and Visit Reminder Texts
recommendations.why: Customers get the update before they think to call. The office stops relaying messages between customers and technicians who are mid-job.

recommendations.title: Repair the Scheduling-to-Accounting Sync
recommendations.tool: Existing Jobber to QuickBooks Online integration
recommendations.why: Invoices flow to accounting automatically, which removes the daily re-entry and the month-end mismatches it causes.
recommendations.setup: Half a day, including one week of reconciliation checks

recommendations.title: Missed-Call Text-Back
recommendations.tool: Auto-reply feature from the business phone provider
recommendations.why: Every unanswered caller gets an instant text with a booking link, so urgent callers have a reason to wait instead of calling a competitor.
recommendations.saved: Recovers callers who would otherwise hang up

recommendations.title: Maintenance Plans as Recurring Jobs
recommendations.tool: Recurring jobs and automated reminders in the scheduling tool
recommendations.why: Moving plans out of the spreadsheet means tune-ups and renewals are scheduled and reminded automatically, even in the busiest weeks.
recommendations.setup: 2 to 3 days to migrate about 350 plans
recommendations.saved: Protects about $6,000 a year in plan revenue

recommendations.title: Same-Day Quotes with Automatic Follow-Up
recommendations.tool: Quote templates on a tablet plus automatic quote follow-ups
recommendations.why: Quotes go out from the driveway instead of the kitchen table, and follow-ups happen without anyone remembering to send them.

quick_wins_plan.task: Turn on visit reminders and "on my way" texts
Set up missed-call text-back with a booking link
Repair the accounting sync and start reconciliation checks
Build install quote templates and turn on quote follow-ups

next_steps: Migrate maintenance plans into recurring jobs before the next renewal cycle
Replace the Monday spreadsheet with a saved report in the scheduling tool
Review after one busy-season month: missed calls, status calls, sync errors
assumptions: Status calls: 12 per day at about 4 minutes each over 5 days is about 4 hours per week; automated texts are assumed to remove half.
Double entry: the owner's estimate of about 1 hour per day; a working sync is assumed to remove most of it.
Lapsed plans: the operations manager's estimate of about 30 plans at about $200 per year each.
Missed calls: the share of the roughly 40 weekly missed calls that were new customers is unknown, so no revenue is claimed for recommendation 3.
Feature availability depends on the current plan tier of each tool and has not been verified in this sample run.
